status: DECLARED before the governing leave-one-month-out run (tools/run_pop_signals.py --declaration configs/pop_signals_v2.json); the month-level diagnostic and a single-seed scratch read that motivated it are disclosed below; an eight-seed scratch read of the same feature sets was running at declaration time and had produced no result yet
purpose: The v9 population classifier carries the calendar month as a feature, so on the ranking it applies July 2025's fill propensity (the lowest of 2025: 32% of population rows) to July 2026 and January 2025's (41%) to January 2026. A label-free measure of the airport's record-capture state exists in every file: the share of LIRF arrivals whose in-block equals their scheduled arrival (within v9's 120 s fill tolerance). Across the twelve 2025 months it tracks the population's departure fill share with r = 0.81 (July 2025 the lowest on both: 0.135 / 0.317; February-March and December the highest: 0.17-0.19 / 0.75-0.77). The ranking's arrival shares are 0.146 (January 2026, like January 2025's 0.148) and 0.156 (July 2026, well above July 2025's 0.135 and in the range of August-December 2025, whose population fill shares were 0.43-0.77). This round gives the classifier that share (and, as a variant, drops the calendar month so the propensity is read from the share rather than from the month), on top of the previous-arrival identity features of configs/pop_signals_v1.json.

control.description: v9's seventeen classifier features, the same protocol and seed bag (identical to configs/pop_signals_v1.json's control)

pa.description: configs/pop_signals_v1.json's pa, the v42 export's candidate; re-scored here as the reference

pa_arrm.description: pa + arr_fill_m (the month's LIRF arrival fill share), calendar month kept

pa_arrm_nomonth.description: pa + arr_fill_m with the calendar month feature removed

arrm_nomonth.description: v9's features with the calendar month replaced by arr_fill_m (no previous-arrival features)

pa_arrd.description: pa + arr_fill_m + arr_fill_d (the UTC day's arrival fill share; within-month day variation looked weak: fill 0.44-0.53 across quintiles)

feature_definitions.arr_fill_m: share of the file's LIRF arrivals in the row's calendar month whose in-block is within 120 s of their scheduled arrival (src/prc2026_final/pop_signals.arrival_fill_shares); in a leave-one-month-out fold the held-out month's own arrivals give its share, as the ranking file's arrivals do for 2026
feature_definitions.arr_fill_d: the same share over the row's UTC day

scope: population rows with a schedule interval at or below the mixture threshold (43,200 s), as configs/pop_signals_v1.json
protocol: as configs/pop_signals_v1.json: leave-one-month-out over the twelve 2025 months, classifier and normal component fitted on the other eleven months, mixture on the held-out rows, squared error against the held-out label

rule.selection: unchanged from configs/pop_signals_v1.json: among candidates at least 3% below the control's twelve-month in-scope SSE, better in at least 8 of 12 months, with the paired-month bootstrap 95% interval below zero, the lowest SSE; otherwise nothing
rule.note: the same rule failed pa by one month (7 of 12) in v1; the report also states each candidate's change excluding the one June one-day row and its January / July readings (the ranking months' analogs), for the user's decision

export: as configs/pop_signals_v1.json (v40 + 0.75 x (mixture_selected - mixture_v9_shipped) on the in-scope ranking population rows, floor -12 s); a v43 would replace v42 (the pa export, built at the user's word, not uploaded) rather than stack on it

prior_exploration_disclosed.day_level: population fill share by quintile of the day's arrival fill share 0.35 -> 0.62, but within a month (share minus the month's) only 0.45 / 0.48 / 0.44 / 0.53 / 0.52: the signal is the month's level
prior_exploration_disclosed.single_seed_lomo: base + arr_fill_m + a same-month operator arrival fill rate (10:30 UTC scratch, calendar month kept): 18.591e9 against 18.941e9, unstable by month (January -22%, December +22%)
